summary: A man posted nonconsensual deepfake pornographic images of prominent Australian women on a website and defied removal orders. Australia's Federal Court fined him $343,500 in a first-of-its-kind case under the Online Safety Act.
technical_summary: Generative deepfake/face-swap tools were used to create explicit synthetic images of real women, which were posted on a deepfake porn site. The harm came from deliberate misuse; enforcement followed regulator action and a contempt finding.

summary: A university student submitted AI-generated deepfake videos of themselves for Spanish coursework. The university's board found this to be cheating, annulled the work and suspended the student for a year.
technical_summary: Deepfake face and synthetic voice tools were used to fabricate oral-presentation videos. Mismatched lip movement, an artificial voice and inconsistent language ability exposed the fabrication. Existing assessment processes were not designed to detect synthetic media.

summary: An unidentified attacker used an AI-driven penetration-testing tool together with large language models to breach South Korean financial organizations and steal data. The number of affected institutions is unconfirmed.
technical_summary: ARTEX, an open-source agentic pentesting tool, was combined with LLMs guided by Chinese-language prompts to automate intrusion into bank systems, including a broker inquiry service and an employee mobile system. Exposed attacker directories revealed the tooling.

summary: A network of 17 TikTok accounts used AI-generated voices to narrate conspiracy videos about celebrities and public figures, drawing hundreds of millions of views.
technical_summary: Text-to-speech and voice-cloning tools, including ElevenLabs, generated realistic narration and fake statements imitating a former U.S. president for roughly 5,000 videos. The content spread false claims at low cost and scale on TikTok.

summary: A fraudster reportedly used AI face-modification in video calls to pose as holders of FTX bankruptcy claims, defrauding two companies of over $5.6 million.
technical_summary: Deepfake-style face-changing tools masked the perpetrator's identity during due-diligence video calls, combined with forged IDs and genuine claim data. Funds were then laundered through crypto exchanges. Some conclusions in the investigation are described as evidence-backed guesses.

summary: Instagram used a user's post containing a violent rape threat, which she had shared to highlight online abuse, as an advertisement to her friends and family on Facebook.
technical_summary: An automated system selected an apparently engaging user post to promote Instagram, without detecting the abusive text embedded in the image. The system likely optimized for engagement and lacked content screening for ad use.

summary: Attackers advertised fake AI video-generation websites on social media to trick users into downloading malware that steals credentials and cryptocurrency and can give remote access.
technical_summary: Fake sites imitating tools such as Luma Dream Machine promoted via Facebook groups asked users to upload media, then delivered a ZIP file with a loader, Noodlophile Stealer and sometimes the XWorm RAT. AI served as a social-engineering lure rather than as the attack mechanism.

failure_mode.quote: cybercriminals have uncovered a potent new lure: fake AI platforms promising cutting-edge content generation in exchange for user uploads

harm_type.quote: designed to harvest browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and sensitive data

notes: The malware campaign uses AI only as a lure.

summary: A scammer emailed a deepfake video using a cloned voice of a Salt Lake City police chief, falsely claiming the recipient owed nearly $100,000 to the federal government. Police issued a warning.
technical_summary: Voice-cloning was combined with repurposed footage of a prior TV interview to impersonate the police chief, sent from a spoofed non-official email account. Audio artifacts and the sender domain exposed the fake. No loss was reported.

failure_mode.quote: AI is giving scammers a more convincing way to impersonate police, reports show.

notes: Attempt was recognised as fake; no victim loss reported.

summary: Discord's automated safety system wrongly banned more than 8,000 accounts that posted harmless images such as grids and chessboards. Discord attributed it to a bug and later reinstated everyone affected.
technical_summary: An automated image-matching moderation system produced false positives. A bug converted temporary upload restrictions pending human review into full account bans and blocked automatic reinstatement after staff cleared the accounts.

failure_mode.quote: Discord says a bug affecting its safety system caused it to mistakenly ban more than 8,000 accounts since May.

summary: A systematic review found that none of the machine-learning models for detecting or predicting COVID-19 from chest scans were fit for clinical use because of methodological flaws and biases.
technical_summary: Reviews of hundreds of 2020 COVID-19 imaging models found small, single-source datasets, reused training and testing data, missing external validation and poor documentation. These flaws give misleadingly strong performance and limit generalization.
systems: COVID-19 chest X-ray and CT detection and prognosis models

failure_mode.quote: Our review finds that none of the models identified are of potential clinical use due to methodological flaws and/or underlying biases

lifecycle_stage.quote: some even reused the same data for training and testing

notes: Research-quality concern; no specific patient harm documented.

summary: Staff from the Department of Government Efficiency reportedly fed short grant descriptions into ChatGPT to label National Endowment for the Humanities grants as DEI, then used the results to cancel over $100 million in awards.
technical_summary: A general-purpose LLM was prompted with a one-line DEI yes/no question on web-sourced summaries and its unvetted outputs informed a termination list of about 1,477 grants. Classification was sweeping and sometimes arbitrary, with no meaningful human review.

sector.quote: used ChatGPT to determine whether previously approved National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) grants should be canceled

summary: Figma disabled its AI Make Design feature after it produced near-replicas of Apple's Weather app, raising concerns about copying and legal risk for designers.
technical_summary: The feature used off-the-shelf large language and image models with a commissioned design system and produced low-variability layouts resembling an existing app. Figma denied training on app designs and acknowledged that QA had been rushed.

technology.quote: Make Design uses off-the-shelf large language models

failure_mode.quote: the quality assurance work that should accompany new additions seems to have been overlooked

notes: Whether underlying models were trained on Apple designs is unresolved.
